youtube.aciklama: Residual inhibition is a temporary reduction or disappearance of tinnitus after masking noise stops. In a common protocol, noise is presented 10 dB above the minimum masking level, or MML, for 60 seconds. Many people show partial or complete residual inhibition, but the effect usually lasts seconds to minutes and does not mean a lasting treatment.

cumleler: Can tinnitus briefly vanish when masking noise stops?
The minimum masking level, or MML, is the lowest noise covering tinnitus.
Noise is presented 10 decibels above the MML for 60 seconds.
When it stops, tinnitus may briefly fade or disappear.
This is residual inhibition; it usually lasts seconds to minutes.
Tinnitus can be briefly suppressed; this is not a lasting treatment.
